A graph that has been paying attention

200 travelers, 5,000 places across six kinds of terrain, and a two-layer Graph Attention Network that learned which of them belong together. Every number below comes from that trained model — nothing here is placeholder.

Places by kind
Training loss 30 epochs · mean squared embedding norm
Model spec
input  [type, lat, lon, rating]  (4 features / node)
layer 1 GATConv(4→64, heads=2) → ReLU (head 1: spatial · head 2: type)
layer 2 GATConv(128→64) (64-d node embedding)
score  cosine(user, place) + 0.1 × type_frequency

Ask a traveler where to go next

Pick any of the 200 synthetic users. The model ranks all 5,000 places by embedding similarity, nudges the score toward kinds of places that user already favors, and explains its top picks.

The graph underneath

A sampled neighborhood of the bipartite graph: a handful of users (rings), the places they visited (shapes), and the nearest-neighbor edges between those places. Positions come from a force layout run once per sample.
